title: Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Singaporean men smoking rates
sections.summary: Twenty-three percent of Singaporean men smoke, higher than Australia and the US, and six die daily from smoking-related diseases.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Twenty-three percent, or one in four, Singaporean men still smoke, much higher than in countries, such as Australia, which stands at 14.5% and the US at 15.6%.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Every day, six Singaporeans die prematurely from smoking-related diseases.

sections.label: Minimum legal age increase
sections.summary: The MLA will rise over three years to 19 in 2019, 20 in 2020 and 21 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The MLA will be progressively raised over a period of three years to minimise impact on smokers currently between the ages of 18 and 21.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We plan to raise the MLA to 19 on 1 January 2019, 20 on 1 January 2020 and, finally, to 21 on 1 January 2021.

sections.label: Ban on emerging tobacco products
sections.summary: The Bill prohibits importation, sale, distribution, purchase, use and possession of emerging and imitation tobacco products.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Effectively, the importation, sale, distribution, purchase, use and possession of emerging and imitation tobacco products shall be prohibited with this Bill.

sections.label: Great Britain e-cigarette use
sections.summary: An estimated 2.8 million adults in Great Britain used e-cigarettes in 2016, four times the 700,000 users in 2012.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: For example, an estimated 2.8 million adults in Great Britain used e-cigarettes in 2016, representing a four-fold increase from 700,000 users in 2012.

sections.label: E-cigarette users becoming smokers
sections.summary: A review of nine US studies found e-cigarette users were three times more likely to become cigarette smokers than non-users.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: A systematic review of nine studies involving more than 17,000 youths in the United States found that e-cigarette users were three times more likely to become cigarette smokers compared to non-users.

sections.label: ENDS harm reduction arguments rejected
sections.summary: Views that ENDS reduce smoking-related harm were considered but not accepted.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: There are also views that offering a less harmful product like ENDS is a way to reduce the harm of smoking-related diseases in smokers.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We have considered these arguments, but are not persuaded.

sections.label: ENDS makers submitting cessation data
sections.summary: ENDS manufacturers with supporting data from credible scientific studies can submit products for evaluation as smoking cessation therapy.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: If any ENDS manufacturer has supporting data from credible and robust scientific studies, it can submit its product for evaluation as a smoking cessation therapy.

sections.label: Minimum legal age raised to 21
sections.summary: The Bill raises the minimum legal age over three years, to 19, then 20, then 21.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, this Bill proposes to increase the minimum legal age (MLA) over three years to 21 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Twelve months from the day the law is passed, the MLA will be raised to 19.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Then, we have to wait another 12 months for it to go up to 20, and another year before it is raised to the age of 21.

sections.label: Penalties for tobacco offences
sections.summary: First offences carry a fine up to $10,000, jail up to six months, or both; later offences up to $20,000, 12 months, or both.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For a first offence, a fine of up to $10,000, or jail of up to six months or both; and for the second and subsequent offences, a fine of up to $20,000 or jail of up to 12 months or both.

sections.label: Smoking health risks and age 21
sections.summary: Smoking is causally linked to lung cancer, stroke, heart disease, emphysema and chronic bronchitis, and the speaker supports raising the legal smoking age to 21.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It has been causally linked to conditions like lung cancer, stroke, heart disease, emphysema and chronic bronchitis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I support the raising of the legal smoking age to 21 as well as including online transactions under the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) Act.

sections.label: CDC e-cigarette use rise
sections.summary: The US CDC reported e-cigarette use among high school students rose from 1.5% to 16% between 2011 and 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The US CDC has reported that e-cigarette use among high school students between 2011 and 2015 increased by more than 10 times, from 1.5% to 16%.

sections.label: Controlled e-cigarettes for registered smokers
sections.summary: The member asks why registered smokers trying to quit cannot receive a controlled quantity of e-cigarettes for a cessation programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Why not allow a controlled quantity of e-cigarettes to smokers who register with, say, the Health Promotion Board, for a smoking cessation programme and sign a declaration that they are smokers trying to quit?

sections.label: Royal College of Physicians e-cigarette report
sections.summary: A February 2016 British Royal College of Physicians report concluded e-cigarettes are beneficial to public health and much safer than smoking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In a report released in February 2016, which I also referred to earlier this year in this House, the British Royal College of Physicians (RCP) reviewed the clinical evidence and concluded that e-cigarettes are beneficial to public health and much safer than smoking.

sections.label: Cochrane evidence on e-cigarettes
sections.summary: Data suggest e-cigarette risks are unlikely to exceed 5% of smoked tobacco risks, and Cochrane found e-cigarettes can help quit smoking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Although it is not possible to estimate the long-term health risks associated with e-cigarettes precisely, the available data suggest that they are unlikely to exceed 5% of those associated with smoked tobacco products, and may well be substantially lower than this figure." A report from Cochrane, a global non-profit group that reviews all the evidence on healthcare interventions and summarises the findings, came to similar conclusions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I will quote from the report from Cochrane: "While our conclusions are limited because there are not many high quality studies available yet, overall the evidence suggests that one, e-cigarettes with nicotine can help people quit smoking; two, they do not seem to have any serious side effects in the short- to mid- term (up to two years); and three, in some cases, switching to them leads to changes in your blood and breath that are consistent with the changes you would see in people who give up smoking altogether." We can say that the evidence on e-cigarettes is not 100% fool-proof.

sections.label: Smoker access to e-cigarettes
sections.summary: The speaker asks that confirmed smokers be allowed access to e-cigarettes for a period as part of quitting or reducing consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Again, I am not arguing that e-cigarettes be made legal but that we allow confirmed smokers access to e-cigarettes at least for a certain period of time as part of their efforts to quit smoking or reduce consumption.

sections.label: Review evidence and support Bill
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Ministry would review evidence and reconsider, and supports the Bill with reservations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If the Ministry will not change its position, would the Ministry at least agree to review the evidence and re-consider its position if more evidence emerges that e-cigarettes really do reduce harm?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Having said that, Mr Speaker, Sir, I believe the good in this Bill outweighs the bad and I do support the Bill with the reservations mentioned above.

sections.label: Raising legal smoking age to 21
sections.summary: Citing feedback about students smoking in uniform and forming cliques, the speaker supports raising the legal smoking age to 21.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Having received disturbing feedback about students spotted smoking in their school uniforms, or even forming smoking cliques in school and National Service, I am supportive of the Bill to raise the legal smoking age to 21.

sections.label: Australia tobacco purchase age lobbying
sections.summary: Members of Australia's Eliminate Cancer Initiative lobby governments to raise the legal tobacco purchase age from 18 to 21.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, members of the Eliminate Cancer Initiative in Australia are lobbying to convince federal and state governments to raise the legal tobacco purchase age from 18 to 21, which they believe will not only save lives but up to A$3.1 billion a year from the government's coffers.

sections.label: Inadequate enforcement white elephant
sections.summary: The passage states that if enforcement is inadequate, the policy will become a white elephant.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If enforcement is inadequate, the policy will become a white elephant.

sections.label: School counsellors smoking cessation
sections.summary: The passage asks whether schools have counsellors trained in smoking cessation, as they have counselling and career guidance professionals.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Just as we now have professionals in counselling and career guidance stationed in schools to meet changing demands of the youth population, are there counsellors in schools who are trained in smoking cessation?

sections.label: Support raising minimum smoking age
sections.summary: The passage supports raising the minimum smoking age to 21 and hopes the Government will reduce Singapore's smoking rate.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):    Smoking damages the health of our young people.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, I fully support the amendment to increase the minimum smoking age to 21.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Besides upping the smoking age, I hope the Government can also think of ways to bring down the smoking rate in Singapore.

sections.label: Report smokers and help students
sections.summary: The passage says the public should report smokers via OneService or a hotline, and schools should help addicted students quit.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The public should be able to report these smokers via OneService or a designated hotline.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If the school finds out that a student is addicted, it should not just punish him but also find experts to help him quit smoking.

sections.label: Smoking near window and phasing
sections.summary: The passage suggests prohibiting smoking near windows and says raising the age at once would have been better than over three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Such measures may include prohibiting the smoker from smoking near the window.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I think it would have been better, however, that we increase it as soon as possible, instead of incrementally over three years.

sections.label: Remove gradual phasing appeal
sections.summary: The passage says the schedule is hard to track and may tempt exempted youths, appealing to remove gradual phasing and raise the age at once.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is not easy for the man-in-the-street to keep track of the schedule and, even worse, this arrangement may tempt certain youths who are exempted to try their first smoke earlier, since they enjoy the so-called unique chance to be among the last batch of those who get to smoke legally below the age of 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, I appeal to the Minister to seriously consider removing the gradual phasing and raise the legal age in one swift stroke.

sections.label: Smoking rate and costs
sections.summary: Despite fairly high costs, about 13% of Singaporean residents smoke.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Despite their fairly high costs, we still have a pretty high number of smokers − roughly about 13% of Singaporean residents smoke.

sections.label: Reducing licensed tobacco retailers
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Ministry how many licensed retailers exist and whether outlets can be reduced by about 5% yearly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is imperative that we drastically reduce the availability of these toxic products.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And, I would like to ask the Ministry how many licensed retailers there are presently and if we can aim to reduce these outlets, in phases, if necessary, say, by about 5% every year.

sections.label: Smoking disease burden rank
sections.summary: Cigarette smoking is the second highest risk factor contributing to Singapore's disease burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Cigarette smoking is the second highest risk factor contributing to the burden of disease in Singapore.

sections.label: Minimum legal age and phasing
sections.summary: The MLA was raised to 21 because most smokers first experiment before that age, but the speaker questions a phased approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The MLA has been raised to 21 in response to the statistics that show that the majority of smokers have their first experimentation before that age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Yet, I am confused as to why we should decide on a phased approach to this.

sections.label: Small study and complete ban
sections.summary: The speaker doubts a small initial study justifies exceptions and asks why a complete ban is not considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, I am highly doubtful that an initial study conducted with a very small group of respondents can be relied on for us to make exceptions to the rules that we are setting here today in this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I, therefore ask, why we should not be considering a complete ban on a product that we deem as having no benefit.

sections.label: Support for TCASA amendments
sections.summary: The speaker calls for an eventual tobacco ban but supports the TCASA amendments raising the MLA and banning tobacco substitutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I, therefore, add my voice to call for the Ministry to consider all the possibilities to lead to an eventual ban on tobacco in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But, that being said, with the current proposals in this TCASA, I support the amendments to the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Increasing the MLA for smoking from 18 to 21 is a move in the right direction and making it an offence to own tobacco substitutes, such as e-cigarettes, will surely prevent potential addiction to those substitutes.

sections.label: Young adults and nicotine addiction
sections.summary: Research shows young adults are less likely to start or become addicted to nicotine after age 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Research has shown that young adults would be less likely to start or be addicted to nicotine after the age of 21.

sections.label: Financial penalties for cigarette sales
sections.summary: Progressively harsher financial penalties could help ensure cigarettes are not sold to underage teens and reduce access to social sources.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Introducing financial penalties that will progressively get harsher could be one way in which the state can not only ensure cigarettes are not sold to underage teens, but also ensure a reduction in access to social sources.

sections.label: War on Smoking proposal
sections.summary: HPB could consider a War on Smoking to stop this social ill, mitigate rising healthcare costs and reduce environmental risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similar to the "War on Diabetes", HPB could consider a "War on Smoking" to stop this social ill and to mitigate against rising healthcare costs in the long run and reduce the environmental risks smoking poses.

sections.label: Raising minimum smoking age to 21
sections.summary: Surveys show smokers under 30 fell from 16% to 13%, but about 80% of youth who smoked became hooked before 21, so the speaker supports raising the minimum age from 18 to 21.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Data from the national health surveillance surveys conducted in 2010 and 2013 have shown that the number of smokers below the age of 30 years old has dropped from 16% to about 13% from 2010 to 2013.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, according to HPB, the proportion of youth that picked up smoking and who then became hooked on smoking before the age of 21, remains high at about 80%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I support the amendments to this Bill that will raise the minimum age for the sale or purchase of cigarettes and other tobacco products from 18 to 21.

sections.label: Smoking and illegal drug risk
sections.summary: A 2000 Johns Hopkins study shows cigarette smoking increases a person's risk of using illegal drugs, with smokers more likely to have tried marijuana, cocaine, crack and heroin.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A comprehensive study published in 2000 from the Johns Hopkins School of Public Health shows that "cigarette smoking increases a person's risk of using illegal drugs" and that, "For all age groups combined, the 65.8% of participants who had ever smoked were: seven times more likely to have tried marijuana; seven times more likely to have tried cocaine; 14 times more likely to have tried crack; and 16 times more likely to have tried heroin.

sections.label: Cheap roll-your-own tobacco packets
sections.summary: A packet of loose tobacco leaves or Roll-Your-Own Tobacco found in many mom-and-pop shops contains about five to 10 cigarette papers and costs only $2.60.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: This is a packet of loose tobacco leaves or "Roll-Your-Own Tobacco" that we can find in a lot of mom-and-pop shops here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: I think there are about five to 10 pieces of cigarette paper in here, and it is very cheap, costing only $2.60 a packet.

sections.label: Students selling drug-laced cigarettes
sections.summary: Enterprising students in Institutes of Higher Learning mix loose tobacco leaves with weed and sell them as drug-laced cigarettes to schoolmates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: A few of our very enterprising students in our Institutes of Higher Learning are mixing such loose tobacco leaves with weed and selling them as drug-laced cigarettes to their schoolmates.

sections.label: Malay youth smoking and amendment Bill
sections.summary: Malay youths who smoke daily are about 30% against a national average of 12.7%, so the speaker supports the amendment Bill on cigarette advertisement and sale, especially for those under 21.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Malay youths who smoke daily are about 30%, whereas the national average is only 12.7%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Therefore, I strongly support the amendment Bill on advertisement and sale of cigarettes and smoking accessories, especially to our young people who are under 21 years old.

sections.label: Raising minimum smoking age to 21
sections.summary: The speaker asked why raising the minimum age to 21 was not in that Bill, and is heartened it is in this Bill, increasing the minimum legal smoking age from 18 to 21.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And I asked why the proposal to raise the minimum age, 21 years old, was not included in that Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened to see that it is included in this Bill and that we will be increasing the minimum legal age of smoking from 18 to 21.

sections.label: Research on e-cigarettes for quitting
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Parliamentary Secretary to clarify whether, besides the HSA preliminary research mentioned by Senior Minister of State Amy Khor in March 2017, any detailed research or study has been done on e-cigarettes or other reduced-risk products as a means to help smokers quit as an alternative step-down from traditional cigarettes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary clarify whether other than the preliminary research by HSA mentioned by Senior Minister of State Amy Khor in March 2017, any detailed research or study has been done on the potential of such e-cigarettes or other reduced-risk products as a means to assist smokers to quit smoking as an alternative step-down from traditional cigarettes?

sections.label: Reduced-risk tobacco products and quitting
sections.summary: Mr Daniel Yap shared through a Facebook comment that research has shown allowing alternative reduced-risk tobacco products is an effective means for smokers to quit, and the United Kingdom, New Zealand and most states in the United States have conducted studies and endorsed policy approaches allowing such products for gradually quitting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Through a Facebook comment, Mr Daniel Yap shared with me that research has shown that allowing alternative reduced-risk tobacco products has been proven to be an effective means for smokers to quit smoking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that the United Kingdom, New Zealand and most states in the United States have conducted studies and endorsed policy approaches which allow for alternative reduced-risk tobacco products as ways for smokers to gradually quit the habit of smoking.

sections.label: Plans for in-depth e-cigarette studies
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Parliamentary Secretary to clarify whether there are plans to conduct in-depth studies on potential ways to use e-cigarettes to help smokers quit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary clarify whether there are plans to conduct in-depth studies on potential ways to use such e-cigarettes as a means to help smokers quit?

sections.label: Raising minimum smoking age
sections.summary: The speaker says raising the minimum legal smoking age from 18 to 21 over three years is reasonable and a setback to guard against.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is a setback that we have to guard against.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I think that raising the minimum legal age of smoking from 18 to 21 over three years is reasonable.

sections.label: Effectiveness of smoking measures
sections.summary: The member asks the Parliamentary Secretary to share how effective current measures have been in reducing smoking prevalence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In view of the existing measures to control smoking, I would like to ask the Parliamentary Secretary if he can share with the House how effective the current measures have been in reducing the prevalence of smoking.

sections.label: Enforcing tobacco import ban
sections.summary: The member asks how the ban on unauthorised imports of tobacco products can be enforced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Next, I am curious how we can enforce the ban on unauthorised imports of tobacco products.

sections.label: Smoking at windows and lifts
sections.summary: The member says smokers smoking at home at windows and in lifts affect non-smoking neighbours, as pointed out by Mr Yee Chia Hsing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Another issue which we need to address is that of smokers smoking at home at their windows and in lifts, affecting their non-smoking neighbours, as pointed out by hon Member Mr Yee Chia Hsing.

sections.label: Falling smoking rates
sections.summary: Smoking rates fell from 18% in 1992 but remained at about 12%-14% for the last decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Our smoking rates have fallen from 18% in 1992 but they have remained at about 12%-14% for the last decade.

sections.label: HPB youth cessation programmes
sections.summary: Since 2015, HPB's smoking cessation programmes reached over 4,400 youths, and in 2016 educational programmes reached close to 50,000 youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Since 2015, HPB's smoking cessation programmes have reached out to more than 4,400 youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: HPB conducts additional educational programmes in schools and, in 2016, we reached out to close to 50,000 youths.

sections.label: WHO on e-cigarettes
sections.summary: The World Health Organization does not recognise e-cigarettes as a legitimate cessation aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The World Health Organization does not recognise e-cigarettes as a legitimate cessation aid.

sections.label: HSA prosecutions of vaporiser sellers
sections.summary: Since 2012, HSA has prosecuted 14 sellers of e-cigarettes and other types of vaporisers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Since 2012, HSA has prosecuted 14 sellers of e-cigarettes and other types of vaporisers.

sections.label: Tobacco retailers hiring young employees
sections.summary: A survey of tobacco retailers found 5% currently hire employees aged 18 to 21 to sell tobacco products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: We have also conducted a survey among tobacco retailers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: We have found that 5% of retailers currently hire employees who are aged 18 to 21 to sell tobacco products.

sections.label: Fines for underage tobacco offences
sections.summary: Giving tobacco to an underage person can be fined up to $1,000, and buying for them up to $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: You can be fined up to $1,000 for giving tobacco products to an underage person, and up to $5,000 for buying for them.

sections.label: Ang Hoon loose tobacco monitoring
sections.summary: Ang Hoon and other loose tobacco leaf products were under 2% of 2016 tobacco imports, and MOH will keep monitoring youth use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Although Ang Hoon and other loose tobacco leaf products make up less than 2% of all tobacco imported in 2016, MOH will continue to monitor their use among youths and act accordingly.

sections.label: Decline in tobacco retailers
sections.summary: The number of tobacco retailers declined from 5,555 in 2012 to 4,663 as at 30 September 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The number of tobacco retailers has declined from 5,555 in 2012 to 4,663 as at 30 September 2017.

sections.label: Tobacco control strategy aims
sections.summary: The strategy aims to significantly reduce tobacco use prevalence and does not rule out a complete ban at very low levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Our tobacco control strategy aims to reduce the prevalence of tobacco use significantly over time and, in the longer term, we do not rule out banning tobacco completely when tobacco use is at very low levels.

sections.label: MLA aims to denormalise tobacco
sections.summary: With increased MLA, the aim is to reduce youth temptation, denormalise tobacco use and protect young people from nicotine addiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: With the increase in MLA, we aim to reduce opportunities for youths to be tempted to take up smoking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Our aim is to ultimately denormalise tobacco use and protect our young from being lured into a lifetime of nicotine addiction.

sections.label: Small 18 to 21 cohort
sections.summary: The passage asks why not introduce it now if the 18 to 21 group is small, estimated around 4,000 per birth cohort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: But if it is a relatively small number between the ages of 18 and 21, why not introduce it now?

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: We estimate the numbers to be around 4,000 per birth cohort.

sections.label: Studies, evidence and Health Products Act
sections.summary: Counter studies and criticisms were explained, but evidence can still be submitted under the Health Products Act and exempted if qualifying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: With regard to the three studies, I have explained in my response the counter studies or criticisms of the studies that were made and this is the Cochrane Review, as well as the Royal Physicians Report, that were cited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: But, in any case, the door is still open for them to submit their evidence to be considered under our Health Products Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: And if they qualify as a smoking cessation therapy, it will be exempted from the Tobacco Act.
